item.title: Paper: Leto: Utility-Centric Agent Memory
item.description: This paper introduces a memory system for LLM agents that prioritizes information based on its actual utility for future responses rather than just recording past conversation history.

item.title: Paper: LoomKV: Lossless KV Cache Compression from GPU Memory to SSD for LLM Serving
item.description: LoomKV enables lossless compression of KV caches for LLM serving, allowing for more efficient memory usage across GPUs and SSDs without sacrificing model output quality.

item.title: Paper: CoT-Proxy: Cross-Format Transfer for Distilling Long-Horizon Policies
item.description: The authors demonstrate that long-horizon agents can be effectively trained using only teacher actions, bypassing the need for proprietary chain-of-thought data from closed models.

item.title: Paper: Auditing the Judge: Human-Derived Bias Discovery, Quantification, and Mitigation in LLM Judges
item.description: The researchers developed a framework to identify and mitigate human-aligned biases in LLM-based evaluators, improving the reliability of automated model assessment pipelines.

item.title: Paper: Decision Models for Multilingual Emotion Classification: A Comparative Study Against LLMs and Encoders
item.description: This study compares specialized decision models against standard LLMs for multilingual emotion classification, offering data scientists a faster, more robust alternative to traditional fine-tuned encoders.

item.title: Paper: SUAF: Spectral Universal Advantage Features for Zero-Shot Policy Improvement
item.description: The authors introduce a method to improve reinforcement learning agents by isolating key statistical dependencies, helping practitioners build more reusable and efficient task-independent representations.

item.title: Paper: Decision Columns as an Index: Interpretable Embeddings for Explainable Entity Matching and Search
item.description: This paper proposes using model-generated decision answers as interpretable embeddings, allowing data scientists to perform entity matching and search with better transparency and easier updates.

item.title: Paper: Beyond Self-Critique: Epistemic Convergence Control for Multi-Agent Research Verification
item.description: The authors present a framework to improve multi-agent verification by preventing bias and optimizing compute, which helps practitioners get more reliable results from automated research agents.

item.title: Paper: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
item.description: The authors created a framework that uses AI agents to play-test and iteratively refine game designs, helping developers automate the tuning process for better player engagement.

item.title: Paper: Bio-PM-Guided Synthetic IMU Generation
item.description: This study uses a pretrained biosignal encoder to generate synthetic sensor data, offering a cost-effective way to improve human activity recognition models without collecting new physical data.

item.title: Paper: Represented but misread: Post-training changes how language models read out what they represent
item.description: Researchers found that post-training makes language models worse at utilizing their internal knowledge for specific tasks, suggesting that fine-tuning alters how models interpret their own representations.

item.title: Paper: Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation (ROGUE-AI)
item.description: The authors introduce a framework to systematically replicate and investigate security failures in AI agents, providing a standardized way to diagnose the root causes of autonomous system errors.

item.title: Paper: Jailbreak Detection on Large Language Models via Contrastive Prototype Structures
item.description: The researchers developed a method to detect harmful LLM prompts by comparing them against safety prototypes, offering a data-efficient alternative to training complex downstream classifiers.

item.title: Paper: Who are you? The Personal Imitation Game

item.title: Paper: Ground, Iterate, Trace: Decomposing AI Research Ideation
item.description: The authors created an agentic framework that uses knowledge graphs and creative reasoning operators to help researchers generate more grounded and novel scientific ideas.

item.title: Paper: Auditing black-box clinical prediction models with a large language model through queries alone: a blinded test with planted flaws
item.description: This paper evaluates whether LLMs can reliably audit clinical models for errors, finding that their ability to detect specific, planted flaws in black-box systems is limited.
